clue.text: Young women good enough for writer

parts.note: gals is an informal word for girls or young women
worthy means deserving, of a good enough standard

explanation.surface: Some young women are judged to measure up to an author's standards.
explanation.definitionFit: John Galsworthy was the English novelist who wrote The Forsyte Saga.

clue.text: Good old politician effortlessly making speech

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, the British party that merged into the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: A decent former politician gives a smooth address.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone glib talks fluently and smoothly, often too easily to be trusted.

clue.text: European has drink, finishing with the same again

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a cat does
the drink word's own final letter is repeated, giving a second P

explanation.surface: A European has a drink and then orders another of the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lapp is a member of the Sami people of northern Scandinavia.

clue.text: Challenge that place's visitors

definitions.meaning: the sentry's demand to someone approaching in the dark
read literally, the people who go to that place

explanation.surface: Questioning the people who visit a certain spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry's challenge asks the identity of anyone approaching, and literally names whoever travels to a spot.

clue.text: Cook a sort of meat

definitions.meaning: a joint of meat cooked in the oven, as in Sunday lunch

explanation.surface: An instruction to prepare some meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook in dry heat, and a roast is a joint so cooked.

clue.text: Don't surrender stronghold when given hard offer

parts.note: to hold is to keep possession and not give up
a fort is a fortified stronghold
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A garrison is urged not to give up its fortress even when given a tough ultimatum.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLD FORT together means keep the stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold forth can mean to put forward or present, as an offer or proposal.

clue.text: Book that takes a couple of seconds

parts.note: two words for a second: MO, a moment, and S, the abbreviation for second
two words for a second: MO, a moment, and S, the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A volume that can be read in no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the books of the Old Testament, named after a minor prophet.

clue.text: Notes girl taking drink given by man

indicators.note: taking means the girl's name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name
gin is a spirit
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A girl accepts a drink offered by a man, notes the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like a verb in the surface, but it is the definition; 'given by' simply joins the man to the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginalia are notes or comments written in the margins of a book.

clue.text: Unpleasant bunch's dismissive attitude

parts.note: sour means disagreeable or unpleasant
grapes grow in a bunch

explanation.surface: A nasty group of people has a contemptuous outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: From Aesop's fox, who scorned the grapes he could not reach.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means disparaging something only because one cannot have it.

clue.text: I'm to carry out tests without new lab? Not bloody likely!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the tests word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to probe is to investigate or test

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of lab are made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A scientist doubts they can run experiments without a fresh laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and the definition echoes Eliza Doolittle's famous line in Shaw's Pygmalion.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses that something is very unlikely to happen.

clue.text: Foreign woman cut crime

indicators.note: cut means the word for the crime is docked of its final letter

parts.note: fraud is a crime of deception

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad has her criminal sentence reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter, D, from FRAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German title and word for a married woman, so a woman from abroad.

clue.text: Money got from man in crew

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
of here means belonging to, as a piece of something
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Cash obtained from a sailor on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' suggests a ship, but it is a rowing eight; the man is a playing piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of eight were old Spanish silver dollars, the coins of pirate stories.

clue.text: Existing expenses

parts.note: read literally, the money one must spend simply to exist

explanation.surface: A phrase about the costs one currently faces.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday economic phrase means the price of basic necessities, literally what it costs to stay alive.

clue.text: Where one can lie low

parts.note: not hiding out but literally sleeping close to the floor

explanation.surface: Somewhere to hide away from trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie low' means stay hidden, but here it is literal: a bed set low, stored under another.
explanation.definitionFit: A truckle bed is a low bed on wheels kept under a higher one.

clue.text: War effort, initially, turned out submarine

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged
initially means only the first letter of effort is used

explanation.surface: A war effort that went wrong came about at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WAR, E (first of 'effort') and TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means existing or happening below the sea's surface.

clue.text: Noble art patron well placed to see canvas

definitions.text: Noble art patron well placed to see canvas

parts.words: Noble art patron well placed to see canvas
parts.note: the noble art is boxing and the canvas is the floor of the boxing ring, not a painting

explanation.surface: An art lover has a good seat to view a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble art' and 'canvas' suggest a gallery, but the noble art is boxing, and the canvas is the ring's floor where a knocked-down fighter lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator with a seat right next to the boxing ring has the best view of the action.

clue.text: Hated faulty carriage — such a dangerous vehicle

indicators.note: faulty means broken, so the letters of hated are rearranged

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage

explanation.surface: A despised defective carriage is a hazard on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathtrap is anything, such as an unsafe car, likely to cause a fatal accident.

clue.text: Bow that originally had it

parts.note: refers to the 1920s film star known as the It girl, her surname being Bow

explanation.surface: An archer's weapon that once possessed something.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is not a weapon or ribbon but a surname: the silent-film actress who starred in It (1927) and was the original It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara Bow was the American actress whose 1927 film It made her the first It girl.

clue.text: Reported investigation of European country

indicators.note: reported signals that a word is spoken and we write what is heard

parts.note: a check is an inspection or investigation

explanation.surface: News coverage of an inquiry into some European nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Czech is the adjective for the Czech Republic, the central European country.

clue.text: Work of Praxiteles, terribly atrophied

indicators.note: terribly suggests badly mangled, so the letters of atrophied are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek sculpture has badly wasted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxiteles carved the famous Aphrodite of Knidos, a statue of the Greek goddess of love.

clue.text: Cave below one of the houses

parts.note: lower means further below
a cave is an underground chamber

explanation.surface: An underground cavern lies beneath a dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The houses are houses of a parliament, not homes.
explanation.definitionFit: In a two-part parliament the lower chamber is one house, such as the Commons.

clue.text: Young person's sort of suit

definitions.meaning: someone under the legal age of adulthood
in bridge, clubs and diamonds are the lower-ranking suits

explanation.surface: A youngster's kind of outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is a person under age, and a minor suit in bridge is clubs or diamonds.

clue.text: Body of 6 turned over

indicators.note: turned over means the word is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: the answer at 6 across, the Old Testament book

explanation.surface: A body found under a number six that was overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Soma is the biological term for the body as distinct from the mind or germ cells.

clue.text: Magistrate has drugs put in military vehicle

indicators.note: put in says the drugs go inside the magistrate letters

parts.note: JP stands for Justice of the Peace, a British magistrate
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so two of them make drugs

explanation.surface: A magistrate finds narcotics planted in an army vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The magistrate is a Justice of the Peace, and E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, doubled for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeep is a sturdy four-wheel-drive vehicle first built for the US Army.

clue.text: Out to lunch in clubs

definitions.meaning: an informal phrase for crazy or mad
clubs used to hit a ball, as in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: Someone is away having lunch at their clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is slang for mad, and bats are also the clubs players swing.

clue.text: Runs into criminal simpleton getting bird

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the criminal word

parts.note: bent is slang for crooked or criminal
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a goose is a silly, foolish person

explanation.surface: A fool bumps into a crook and ends up with a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' looks like prison slang for a jail term; it is the definition, a real bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The brent goose is a small dark goose that winters on British coasts.

clue.text: Choice of large numbers for the rest of the pupils

parts.note: D and M are the Roman numerals for 500 and 1000
or is the word that offers a choice
D and M are the Roman numerals for 500 and 1000

explanation.surface: Picking between big figures to decide the remainder of a class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest' is not the remainder but sleep: a dormitory is where boarding pupils rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory is a school's sleeping room, where boarders go to rest.

clue.text: Light with shade?

parts.note: shade read as a ghost or soul, so a light that runs on a ghostly spirit, not one with a lampshade

explanation.surface: A lamp with a shade over it.
explanation.walkthrough: A shade is a spirit, and spirit is also the methylated fuel such a lamp burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit lamp is a small lamp that burns alcohol, called spirit, as fuel.
